home.headline: A learner and builder at heart, I lead by staying close to the work and paying forward everything it has taught me.
home.pitch: I'm Ishita Majumdar. I move fluidly between leading high-impact teams and building hands-on, most recently spending three years building with AI. Staying close to the actual work is how I ensure I learn the very fast evolving AI landscape and deliver real value both for personal and enterprise productivity.

highlights.title: Years in Tech
highlights.text:
My journey spans from engineering cellular infrastructure at Motorola to driving enterprise intelligence as Chief Data and AI Officer today—evolving through every major shift from IP networks to modern AI. Across every decade and technology cycle, my north star has remained unchanged: applying cutting-edge engineering to solve complex, real-world problems for people and enterprises.

We are living through the most extraordinary era in technology history. For builders and leaders, the canvas has never been broader. We have a rare, historic opportunity to build solutions from first principles, lead defining transformations, and solve the fundamental challenges of our time; reimagining productivity, scaling human potential, and building a more intelligent future.

highlights.title: Product Thinking
highlights.text:
I think in terms of products. I start with a problem statement or a customer pain point, then deepen my understanding through discovery and targeted questions. From there, I usually build a functional prototype with AI and synthetic data to show value and get feedback. I keep iterating and testing based on customer input, working closely with design. Eventually I hand it off to engineering to optimize the code and build in scale, resiliency, and reliability.

Honestly, AI has changed how far I take this myself. My role used to stop at understanding requirements and scoping the product. Now I go further, actually building and testing a prototype on my own machine before pushing it to git and hosting it on the cloud.

Having spent years as a PM, scaling and leading a PMO and driving many cross functional initiatives teams, and then leading engineering teams brings my leadership full circle. It taught me that while frameworks, governance, and team alignment are essential for scaling, true product empathy comes from staying directly connected to the build. By pairing hands-on prototyping with strategic oversight, I can mentor teams with greater clarity, compress discovery cycles, and ensure we build products that solve real problems at enterprise scale.

highlights.title: Data - What can it tell?
highlights.text:
To me, data is not just a measure of past performance, it is the bedrock of enterprise strategy and decision intelligence. Ultimately, data-driven insights are not meant for an elite few—they must be democratized across the organization, accessible to every employee through whichever interface or conduit they choose. Any enterprise workers should able to answer...

  • What is happening? Establishing real-time visibility and a single source of truth across complex, cross-functional ecosystems

  • Why is it happening? Uncovering operational friction, systemic root causes, and hidden vulnerabilities before they impact business performance

  • What comes next? Unlocking predictive power—leveraging clean datasets, custom LLMs and Gen AI models to automate decisions, optimize capital allocation and drive proactive strategy

Turning data into business impact requires more than algorithms; it demands rigorous governance, data quality frameworks, and product-focused execution to transform operational data into a primary driver of enterprise value.

highlights.title: Learning AI from first principals
highlights.text:
To me, AI leadership isn’t about sitting at a 30,000-foot level and looking at status reports. Iit’s about knowing how things actually work under the hood so you can lead with clarity. 

My own journey with modern AI started with the fundamentals: downloading Ollama, running open-source models locally, and experimenting in the OpenAI sandbox and plugins to get a feel for capabilities and prompt dynamics.

As the tooling evolved, so did my workflow. I moved into hands-on agentic development with Cursor, Windsurf, and ultimately Claude Code, embracing the shift toward "vibe coding" to turn complex product ideas into working software faster than ever before. For me, staying close to the build means going all the way to production; writing code, pushing to Git, and hosting live apps on Railway so I can share fully functional Web URLs directly with stakeholders for early feedback and user testing.

By actively building at every stage of the technical evolution, I can bridge the gap between early experimentation and real enterprise impact, ensuring our high-level strategy stays firmly anchored in technical reality.

highlights.title: Leading Transformation
highlights.text:
Leading enterprise transformation isn’t just about rolling out new technology, it’s about changing how an organization operates. 

Whether it was aggressively retiring legacy infrastructure to eliminate technical debt, modernizing core platforms to run on open-source frameworks, or agentifying end-to-end workflows to bring real-time intelligence into daily operations, the goal has always been the same: building systems that are resilient, scalable, and fast. For transformations to be a success both adoption and adaption need to occur simultaneously. My job was not done after build, test, deploy. It continued with training, governance, support and increase adoption.

True transformation happens at the intersection of architecture and behavior. It means shifting from rigid, siloed processes to flexible platforms and data-driven decisioning. By establishing unified governance and staying close to the execution, I’ve helped organizations dismantle operational friction, accelerate cycle times, and unlock measurable gains in speed, efficiency, and enterprise agility.

highlights.title: Lessons learned
highlights.text:
Over a 25-year career, our defining insights rarely come from standard resume highlights. I believe true leadership maturity is shaped as much by failures and hard-won learnings as by high-profile wins. Here are the core experiences that have most deeply defined my executive approach.

  1. Early in my leadership career, I spearheaded a critical initiative to achieve six-nines system availability. Fully immersed in technical execution, I went into a C-level review status meeting, confident, until asked about parallel vendor negotiations for our core database infrastructure. I didn't have the answers.

    It was a pivotal wake-up call. I learned, true end-to-end ownership requires total visibility across technical, operational, and commercial workstream. Given a second chance, I unified governance across all streams, delivered the initiative successfully, and fundamentally redefined what complete executive accountability meant for my leadership going forward.

  2. While leading a CEO-prioritized technology transformation, execution was running smoothly under strong PMO governance and rigorous risk frameworks. Then the unexpected happened: a competitor aggressively poached dozens of key engineers from a critical team. It was a classic "unknown unknown" that threatened our entire timeline. We immediately pivoted, built and activated a contingency plan, and protected both our target delivery date and budget. The core takeaway was clear: no matter how airtight your plan is, macro surprises will happen, and true program leadership is defined by how fast you adapt. Keep calm and carry on!

  3. Perhaps the hardest-earned insight of my career is that technical excellence and flawless strategy mean very little without strong organizational trust. Early on, it’s easy to believe that compelling data and execution speed alone will win the day. But real impact is ultimately gated by the strength of your relationships—upward, downward, and across peer networks.

    Building trust and respect at every level takes distinct leadership muscles. Because there’s no universal playbook, navigating these dynamics requires learning how to initiate, cultivate, and maintain authentic relationships on the ground.

biography.title: Who I Am
biography.lede: The LinkedIn version, minus the corporate filter, with a few callouts that never made it onto a resume.
biography.summary:
I’m a rare executive who stepped away from traditional organizational leadership to build with AI from first principles, and that hands-on technical depth is what shapes how I lead today. It started at Huawei’s Central Research Institute, where I worked on the architecture for next-generation, context-aware AI systems. It extended at eBay where we continuously strived for engineering excellence in modernizing data tech stack to be current with new technologies which are not bounded by vendor contracts. It became deeply personal when I co-founded a startup building a human-powered AI platform at the intersection of health, data, and care support for families with special needs. 

As Chief AI officer, I lead global data and AI strategy, building trusted, intelligent systems while driving a culture of data literacy and ethical AI adoption across the enterprise. But I still stay active in the build, not just above it. I regularly use modern AI tools for product design, rapid prototyping, and QA, bringing the same hands-on builder mindset to enterprise leadership that I relied on as a founder.

career.title: Chief Data and AI Officer — Relanto

career.title: Co-Founder / CPTO — Stealth Startup
career.text:
We started this company as three co-founders, inspired by our common experiences as care givers to children/young adults who have neuro-developmental conditions. With the advent of generative AI, we decided to build a prototype using LLM and see if we can build an agent focused on answering questions from families who are struggling to get advice on.... 

What to do when your child has a meltdown and we know she is on the spectrum?

Can I see a private behavioral therapist and not have to wait for 2 months, if I am willing to spend money from my pocket?

Can the government help? How?

Information was fragmented and un trusted. What if we can build a healthcare platform that is an integrated source of information, community, access to medical help and most importantly getting advice from folks who are trusted and experienced?

Product wise, it was great! GTM was it was not too great. It seemed after 2 years, that it should be a non profit

career.title: Vice President, Data Analytics Platforms — eBay
career.meta: Jan 2020 – Mar 2024 · San Francisco Bay Area
career.text:
By this time, I have spent many years in the data space. Enabling big data stack, using open source technology, for customer use cases in the telecom space. Defining and managing data products from Site DB, Data Analytics platforms, Data tools, Data preparation for ML algorithms. Realizing the massive importance of data from ingest to insights for better buyer and seller experience. Acknowledging how hard it is to maintain clean, compliant and trusted data for all consumers. The SQL savvy users: the Developers, the Analysts. The non SQL savvy users like the product managers, sales, business development managers. Increasingly, I believed that Data in any form should be accessible by any enterprise worker - with the right controls and access of course. It should be the Data org's responsibility to make this possible.  Hence it was a natural career transition for me to lead the data organization including data engineers, data scientists and data product managers on this journey to make data and data derivatives - accessible by everyone independently. For this, I added my three steel threads on how to achieve this.

  1. Build an A+ team. I pursued external and internal candidates with equal gusto so that can complement each other in their passion for getting the best out of data. My golden rule: hire no-ego, smart people who can work as a team.
  2. Be accountable for making data work for others. Data consumers should trust the data for any use case
  3. Be transparent with Data measures. That means sit with our customers to jointly determine KPIs and then keep on measuring them and publish the dashboards for all to see. No hiding!

career.title: Global Head of Technology Products — eBay
career.text:
I joined eBay to manage the Data Products from infrastructure to analytics to data tools. My technical expertise was in the data analytics space and very soon extended I learned to understand how experiment platforms work for decision making and how personalization platforms collect behavior signals and deliver "next best action".


How do we build the right platform to collect the true signals and separate from noise? 

How can we conduct faster experiments and better hypothesis testing?

How do we deliver in biweekly sprints and have better output and adoption?

How do we set up the right process for customer escalations?


My portfolio extended over time to include the entire tech stack from metal to ML. Datacenter & Network, Cloud and Security, AI/ML Platform, Developer tools. As I built the team, I realized this will be a unique combination of technical product managers and technical program managers alike. The Product managers were responsible for product vision, strategy, roadmap, customer engagement and stakeholder management. These folks transitioned from engineering careers to become dedicated product managers so they understood the technology, had the domain knowledge to challenge

aiJourney.title: Building With AI
aiJourney.lede: How I got into this, what I've shipped, and where you can go poke at the code.
aiJourney.story:
I'm a rare executive who stepped away from organizational leadership to build with AI from first principles — and that hands-on technical depth is what now shapes how I lead. It started at Huawei's Central Research Institute, shaping the architecture for next-gen, context-aware AI systems, and it became personal when I co-founded a startup building a human-powered, AI platform at the intersection of health, data, and AI — a care support platform for families with special needs.

Today, as Chief Data and AI Officer, I lead global data and AI strategy — building trusted, intelligent systems and championing a culture of data literacy and ethical AI adoption. I still stay in the build, not just above it: using AI tools directly for product design, rapid prototyping, and QA, the same way I did as a co-founder.

books.title: My favorite reads
books.lede: Reading is a constant for me, usually a book every month across fiction and non-fiction. Here are a few favorites that have stayed with me over time and that I continually return to for inspiration.

items.title: Think Again
items.author: Adam Grant
items.summary: This book will shake your core beliefs and give you the courage to try something new.

items.title: The Running Ground
items.author: Nicholas Thompson
items.summary: I am not a runner, married to one, yes but running is not something I like. Yet this book is so much about life through running. It talks bout grit and endurance through some excellent narration on the human story. It was hard to stop reading, as if I was in a reading race myself.

musings.title: My $0.02
musings.lede: No timestamps on purpose — an idea here should read the same whether you find it today or in five years.

items.title: Stay in the build, not just above it
items.body: Executive credibility without hands-on depth becomes theater. The leaders I trust can still read a design doc, ship a prototype, and feel the tradeoffs their teams live with every day.

items.title: AI strategy fails when it never touches a workflow
items.body: Models are not outcomes. Trusted systems, clear data ownership, and one painful process made better beat a roadmap full of demos that never change how people work.

items.title: Customer obsession is a discipline, not a slogan
items.body: Every initiative I drive starts with who feels the result and ends in revenue or efficiency — not in a polished plan that never leaves the slide deck.

items.title: First principles beat borrowed frameworks
items.body: Stepping away from the org chart to build with AI from scratch reset how I lead. You can't govern what you don't understand at the level of the actual system.

items.title: Operating rhythm is a product
items.body: Stronger ways of working — reviews, decision rights, experiment loops — compound faster than any single feature. Treat the cadence like something you design and ship.

trips.story: The local proving ground. Steep, crowded on weekends, and still the climb that resets a week of meetings into something simpler: one foot, then the next.
